questions.question: Which is the most common tidal pattern?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Semi-diurnal tides**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Semi-diurnal tides** are characterized by two high tides and two low tides each day.
 
• This tidal pattern is the most common worldwide, especially along the Atlantic coasts of North America and Europe.
 
• The high and low tides occur approximately every 12 hours and 25 minutes.
 
• Semi-diurnal tides typically have a regular and predictable pattern, making them essential for coastal navigation and marine activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mixed tides:**

 
 
• Mixed tides have characteristics of both semi-diurnal and diurnal tides.
 
• They usually have two high tides and two low tides of different heights each day.
 
• This pattern is common along the Pacific coasts of North America.
 
 
 
• **Diurnal tides:**
 
 
• Diurnal tides have only one high tide and one low tide each day.
 
• This pattern is less common and can be observed in the Gulf of Mexico and parts of Southeast Asia.
 
 
 
• **Spring tides:**
 
 
• Spring tides are not a tidal pattern but rather a condition where tides have the greatest range between high and low water.
 
• They occur during the full moon and new moon phases when the gravitational forces of the moon and the sun align.

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms belongs to the Vaishnava Monasteries of North East India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sattriya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sattriya** is one of the eight classical dance forms of India.
 
• It originated in the **Vaishnava Monasteries of Assam** in North East India.
 
• Sattriya dance was introduced in the 15th century AD by the great Vaishnava saint and reformer **Sankardev**.
 
• It is traditionally performed in the **monasteries known as Sattras** as a part of the rituals and daily worship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi**

 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance form that originated in the state of **Odisha** in eastern India.
 
• It is known for its sensuous and lyrical nature, and the dance is characterized by various bhangas (stances), which involve stamping of the foot and striking various postures as seen in Indian sculptures.
 
 
 
• **Mohiniattam**
 
 
• Mohiniattam is a classical dance form from the state of **Kerala**.
 
• The term Mohiniattam comes from the words 'Mohini' meaning a woman who enchants onlookers and 'attam' meaning graceful and sensuous body movements.
 
• It is performed as a solo recital by women and is known for its graceful movements and feminine themes.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**
 
 
• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form from the state of **Andhra Pradesh** in South India.
 
• It derives its name from the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh and is known for its fast rhythms and fluid movements.
 
• The dance usually begins with an invocation followed by the nritta, nritya, and natya components.

questions.question: How many tiers of government are mentioned in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Constitution of India mentions a **three-tier system of government**.
 
• The three tiers are: **Union Government** (Central Government), **State Governments**, and **Local Governments**.
 
• The **Union Government** deals with subjects of national importance, the **State Governments** deal with state-specific issues, and the **Local Governments** address local level governance.
 
• This three-tier system ensures **decentralization** and effective governance at all levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Government**

 
 
• The Union Government, also referred to as the Central Government, is responsible for governing the entire country.
 
• It is headed by the President of India and the Prime Minister, and it includes various ministries and departments.
 
• It has the power to make laws on subjects enumerated in the Union List as per the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **State Governments**
 
 
• State Governments are responsible for the governance of individual states within India.
 
• Each state has its own government headed by the Governor and the Chief Minister, along with state-specific ministries and departments.
 
• The State Governments have the power to make laws on subjects listed in the State List as per the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Local Governments**
 
 
• Local Governments operate at the grassroots level, addressing local administrative and developmental needs.
 
• The local government system includes Panchayats in rural areas and Municipalities in urban areas.
 
• The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments provided constitutional status to Panchayats and Municipalities, respectively.
 
• Local Governments have the authority to make decisions on local issues and implement development programs at the village, town, or city level.

questions.question: When did the Paris Agreement on Climate Change come into force (become effective from)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4th November 2016**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Paris Agreement on Climate Change is an international treaty that was adopted on 12th December 2015 at the COP21 in Paris.
 
• The agreement aimed to address climate change and its negative impacts by limiting global warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius compared to pre-industrial levels.
 
• It entered into force on 4th November 2016, after being ratified by 55 countries that account for at least 55% of global greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• The agreement includes commitments from all participating countries to reduce their carbon emissions and enhance their climate resilience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paris Agreement**

 
 
• It is a legally binding international treaty on climate change, adopted by 196 parties at COP21 in Paris, on 12 December 2015.
 
• The agreement aims to limit global warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius, preferably to 1.5 degrees Celsius, compared to pre-industrial levels.
 
• It works on a 5-year cycle of increasingly ambitious climate action carried out by countries.
 
• Countries communicate their climate actions known as Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) which outline their efforts to reduce national emissions and adapt to the impacts of climate change.
 
 
 
• **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)**
 
 
• NDCs are at the heart of the Paris Agreement and the achievement of its long-term goals.
 
• Each party to the Paris Agreement is required to establish and communicate ambitious NDCs every five years.
 
• NDCs represent the efforts by each country to reduce national emissions and adapt to the impacts of climate change.
 
 
 
• **Climate Finance**
 
 
• Climate finance refers to local, national, or transnational financing, which may be drawn from public, private, and alternative sources of financing.
 
• It is critical to addressing climate change because large-scale investments are required to significantly reduce emissions and to adapt to the adverse effects and reduce the impacts of a changing climate.
 
 
 
• **Greenhouse Gas Emissions**
 
 
• Greenhouse gases (GHGs) are gases that trap heat in the atmosphere, leading to global warming and climate change.
 
• Common GHGs include carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), and fluorinated gases.
 
• Efforts to reduce GHG emissions are critical to mitigating the impacts of climate change.

questions.question: Who among the following is associated with the Mridangam instrument?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• The mridangam is a percussion instrument from India of ancient origin.
 
• It is the primary rhythmic accompaniment in a Carnatic music ensemble, which is a classical music tradition of South India.
 
• The mridangam is a double-headed drum, with each head producing different tones. It is played with the hands and fingers.

questions.question: According to Census 2011, which group of states have the highest males literacy rates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala and Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kerala** has consistently been known for its high literacy rates, with a strong focus on education and social development.
 
• **Mizoram**, a state in Northeast India, also boasts one of the highest literacy rates in the country, particularly among males.
 
• Both states have implemented various educational reforms and policies aimed at improving literacy and educational standards.
 
• The high literacy rates in these states are indicative of their commitment to education and the effectiveness of their educational policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census 2011**

 
 
• The Census of India 2011 was the 15th National Census of the Country since 1872.
 
• The population enumeration was conducted in two phases: the first phase involved house listing and housing census, and the second phase involved population enumeration.
 
• The literacy rate is defined as the percentage of literate people to the total population aged seven years and above.
 
• The data collected through the census helps in understanding the demographic profile of the country, including literacy rates, population distribution, sex ratio, and other critical indicators.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Rate**
 
 
• Literacy rate is an important indicator of a region's educational status and socio-economic development.
 
• It is typically calculated as the percentage of the population aged seven years and above who can read and write with understanding.
 
• High literacy rates are often associated with better employment opportunities, higher income levels, and improved quality of life.
 
• Government initiatives and policies, such as the Right to Education Act in India, have been instrumental in improving literacy rates across various states.
 
 
 
• **Educational Reforms**
 
 
• Educational reforms refer to the changes and improvements made in the education system to enhance its quality and accessibility.
 
• Such reforms may include curriculum changes, teacher training programs, infrastructure development, and the implementation of new teaching methodologies.
 
• In states like Kerala and Mizoram, educational reforms have played a significant role in achieving high literacy rates and improving overall educational standards.
 
• Efforts to promote inclusive education and provide equal opportunities for all sections of society are critical components of successful educational reforms.

questions.question: According to Census 2011, what was the population density of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**382 persons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census 2011, the population density of India was **382 persons per square kilometer**.
 
• The population density is calculated as the number of people per unit area.
 
• It provides a measure of how crowded a place is.
 
• It helps in understanding the distribution of population across different regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census:**

 
 
• The Census is a process of systematically acquiring and recording information about the members of a given population.
 
• In India, the Census is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• The first complete census of India was conducted in 1881.
 
• The Census collects data on various parameters including population size, distribution, and various demographic, social, and economic characteristics.
 
 
 
• **Population Density:**
 
 
• Population density is a measurement of population per unit area or unit volume.
 
• It is commonly represented as people per square kilometer or square mile.
 
• High population density can indicate high urbanization, whereas low population density might indicate rural or less developed areas.
 
• Population density helps in planning and resource allocation by governments and organizations.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Population Density:**
 
 
• Understanding population density is crucial for urban planning and infrastructure development.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct?

a)The Indian desert lies towards the eastern margins of the Aravali Hills. It is an undulating sandy plain covered with sand dunes.

b) This region has arid climate with low vegetation cover and streams appear during the rainy season.

options.text: Both a and b are correct.
Both a and b are incorrect.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only b is correct.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian desert, also known as the Thar Desert, lies towards the western margins of the Aravali Hills, not the eastern margins.
 
• It is indeed an undulating sandy plain covered with sand dunes.
 
• This region has an arid climate with low vegetation cover.
 
• Streams in the Thar Desert appear only during the rainy season.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thar Desert:**

 
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is a large arid region in the northwestern part of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It forms a natural boundary between India and Pakistan.
 
• The desert extends over an area of about 200,000 square kilometers (77,000 sq mi).
 
 
 
• **Aravali Hills:**
 
 
• The Aravali Range is a range of mountains in western India running approximately 670 kilometers (430 mi) in a south-west direction, starting near Delhi, passing through southern Haryana and Rajasthan, and ending in Gujarat.
 
• It is one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world.
 
 
 
• **Climate of the Thar Desert:**
 
 
• The climate of the Thar Desert is characterized by extreme temperatures, with summer temperatures rising as high as 50°C and winter temperatures dropping below 0°C.
 
• Rainfall is very low, typically ranging between 100 to 500 mm annually.
 
 
 
• **Vegetation in the Thar Desert:**
 
 
• Vegetation is sparse and consists mainly of xerophytic (drought-resistant) plants such as cacti, acacias, and grasses.
 
• During the short rainy season, some ephemeral plants may also grow.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first person in British India to get the scholarship of Indian Society of Oriental Arts, established in 1906?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nandalal Bose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nandalal Bose** was a pioneering Indian painter and a key figure in modern Indian art.
 
• He was a disciple of Abanindranath Tagore, the founder of the Bengal school of art.
 
• Bose was closely associated with the Indian Society of Oriental Art, established in 1906, and was the first recipient of its scholarship.
 
• He is renowned for his contribution to the Indian independence movement through his art, and his works are considered masterpieces of Indian art.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Society of Oriental Art**

 
 
• Founded in 1906, the Indian Society of Oriental Art was established to promote and support Indian art and culture.
 
• It played a crucial role in the revival of traditional Indian art forms during the early 20th century.
 
• The society provided scholarships and support to young artists, fostering the development of a new generation of Indian artists.
 
• It aimed to create an awareness and appreciation of Indian art both in India and internationally.
 
 
 
• **Nandalal Bose's Contributions**
 
 
• Nandalal Bose was instrumental in the design of the Indian constitution's original manuscript, illustrating its pages with images from Indian mythology and history.
 
• He served as the principal of Kala Bhavana, the art school at Visva-Bharati University in Santiniketan, founded by Rabindranath Tagore.
 
• His works include the famous Haripura posters, which were used to inspire and rally people during the Indian independence movement.
 
• In recognition of his contributions, Bose was awarded the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian award, in 1954.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Personalities Mentioned**
 
 
• **Jagdish Chandra Bose**: A pioneering scientist in the field of radio and microwave optics, as well as a biologist who conducted significant research on plant physiology.
 
• **Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar**: An astrophysicist who won the Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on the structure and evolution of stars.
 
• **Prafulla Chandra Roy**: A renowned chemist and founder of Bengal Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals, India's first pharmaceutical company.

questions.question: Which state has two headquarters of Indian Railway Zones?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Uttar Pradesh is the only state in India that has two headquarters of Indian Railway Zones.
 
• The two Railway Zones headquartered in Uttar Pradesh are the North Eastern Railway (NER) with its headquarters in Gorakhpur and the North Central Railway (NCR) with its headquarters in Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad).
 
• The Indian Railways is divided into 18 zones, each with its own headquarters to facilitate smooth and efficient management of railway operations across the country.
 
• Uttar Pradesh's strategic location and vast rail network make it a significant hub for Indian Railways, contributing to its status of having two zonal headquarters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **North Eastern Railway (NER)**

 
 
• The North Eastern Railway (NER) is one of the 18 railway zones in India.
 
• Its headquarters is located in Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh.
 
• NER primarily serves the northeastern states of India and is responsible for the management and operation of railway services in this region.
 
• Gorakhpur railway station in Uttar Pradesh is one of the major stations under this zone.
 
 
 
• **North Central Railway (NCR)**
 
 
• The North Central Railway (NCR) is another important railway zone in India.
 
• Its headquarters is located in Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad), Uttar Pradesh.
 
• NCR covers a large part of North Central India and includes important railway routes connecting the northern and southern parts of India.
 
• Prayagraj Junction is a key railway station under this zone and serves as a major hub for passenger and freight trains.
 
 
 
• **Indian Railways Zones**
 
 
• Indian Railways is divided into 18 zones for administrative convenience and efficient management of railway operations.
 
• Each zone is headed by a General Manager and is further divided into divisions, each headed by a Divisional Railway Manager (DRM).
 
• The zones are responsible for the operation, maintenance, and development of railway infrastructure within their respective regions.
 
• Some of the other important zones include the Western Railway (WR), Eastern Railway (ER), Southern Railway (SR), and Northern Railway (NR).

questions.question: Untouchability is against which of the following fundamental rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to equality**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Right to Equality is one of the six fundamental rights provided by the Constitution of India to its citizens.
 
• It includes equality before the law, prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• It also includes equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and the abolition of untouchability and titles.
 
• The practice of untouchability is a punishable offense under Article 17 of the Indian Constitution, which falls under the Right to Equality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion**

 
 
• It is one of the fundamental rights enshrined in the Indian Constitution under Articles 25 to 28.
 
• It ensures freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.
 
• The state cannot interfere in religious matters, but it can regulate or restrict any economic, financial, political, or other secular activities associated with religious practices.
 
• This right aims to maintain religious harmony and avoid conflicts among different religious groups.
 
 
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies**
 
 
• It is provided under Article 32 of the Indian Constitution and is considered the heart and soul of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
• This right allows individuals to move the Supreme Court or High Courts to seek enforcement of their fundamental rights.
 
• The courts have the power to issue writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari for the enforcement of these rights.
 
• This right ensures the protection and realization of fundamental rights and acts as a guardian of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Right to Liberty**
 
 
• It is part of the Right to Freedom under Articles 19 to 22 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This right guarantees freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• It also includes protection in respect of conviction for offenses, protection of life and personal liberty, and protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.
 
• This right aims to promote individual liberty and protect citizens from arbitrary actions by the state.

questions.question: Elections under which act gave the control of seven provinces in 1937 to the Congress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act, 1935**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1935** was the longest Act passed by the British Parliament, containing 321 sections and 10 schedules.
 
• It provided for the establishment of an **all-India federation** consisting of provinces and princely states.
 
• The Act introduced **provincial autonomy**, allowing provinces to act as separate entities with their own legislative assemblies and governments responsible to the electorate.
 
• Under this act, elections were held in 1937, leading to the Congress party gaining control of seven out of eleven provinces in British India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government of India Act, 1937**

 
 
• There is no such act as the Government of India Act, 1937. The correct act is the Government of India Act, 1935, which was implemented in 1937.
 
 
 
• **Provincial Act, 1935**
 
 
• There is no separate Provincial Act, 1935. The provisions related to provincial autonomy and elections were part of the Government of India Act, 1935.
 
 
 
• **Municipalities Act, 1935**
 
 
• The Municipalities Act, 1935, is not related to the control of provinces. It generally pertains to local governance and municipal administration, not provincial autonomy or elections.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1935**
 
 
• The Government of India Act, 1935, was a crucial step toward greater self-governance in India.
 
• It laid the foundation for the federal structure of government and introduced significant administrative changes.
 
• The Act also sought to address the political demands of Indian leaders by providing a larger role for Indians in governance.
 
• It led to the first provincial elections, which allowed Indian political parties to form governments in their respective provinces, marking a significant shift in colonial administration.

questions.question: Turmeric powder is adulterated with:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**lead chromate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lead chromate is a bright yellow chemical compound and is used as an adulterant to enhance the color of turmeric powder.

• Economic reforms in India were introduced in **1991** due to a severe balance of payments crisis.
 
• The reforms were initiated under the leadership of then Prime Minister **P. V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.
 
• The reforms marked a shift from a mixed economy to a more market-driven economy, focusing on **liberalization, privatization, and globalization**.
 
• These reforms included measures such as reducing import tariffs, deregulating markets, and reducing the role of the government in business.

• **Balance of Payments (BoP) Crisis:**

 
 
• The balance of payments crisis of 1991 was a situation where India was unable to finance its imports or service its external debt obligations.
 
• The crisis led to a sharp decline in foreign exchange reserves, forcing the country to seek a bailout from the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
 
• As a condition for the IMF loan, India had to implement structural reforms to stabilize and liberalize the economy.
 
 
 
• **Liberalization:**
 
 
• Liberalization refers to the relaxation of government restrictions in areas such as trade, industry, and foreign investment.
 
• In India, this meant reducing import tariffs, deregulating markets, and allowing private sector participation in previously restricted areas.
 
 
 
• **Privatization:**
 
 
• Privatization involves transferring ownership or management of enterprises from the public sector to the private sector.
 
• This was aimed at improving efficiency, productivity, and competitiveness of the Indian economy.
 
 
 
• **Globalization:**
 
 
• Globalization refers to the process of integrating the Indian economy with the global economy.
 
• This included measures such as allowing foreign direct investment (FDI), opening up sectors to foreign competition, and promoting exports.

• The Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by law.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**

• It attempted to reduce the power of the judiciary and increase the power of the Parliament.

questions.question: The Charminar was constructed by which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Qutb Shahi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Charminar was constructed in 1591 by the fifth ruler of the Qutb Shahi dynasty, Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
 
• It is located in Hyderabad, Telangana, India, and is one of the most recognized structures of India.
 
• The Qutb Shahi dynasty ruled the Golconda Sultanate in South India from 1518 until its conquest by the Mughal Empire in 1687.
 
• The Charminar is known for its architectural style, which incorporates Persian, Indian, and Islamic influences.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Qutb Shahi Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Qutb Shahi dynasty was founded by Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk, who was originally a Turkic governor of the Bahmani Sultanate in the Deccan region.
 
• The Qutb Shahi rulers were known for their patronage of Persian culture, language, and literature.
 
• They established Hyderabad as their capital and constructed several architectural marvels, including the Golconda Fort and the Charminar.
 
• The dynasty lasted for nearly 170 years before it was annexed by the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb in 1687.
 
 
 
• **Charminar:**
 
 
• The name "Charminar" is derived from two Urdu words: "char" meaning four, and "minar" meaning towers, referring to the four grand arches that support the structure.
 
• It was built to commemorate the end of a deadly plague that had ravaged the city of Hyderabad.
 
• The Charminar is a square structure with each side measuring 20 meters, and it has four grand arches each facing a different direction.
 
• It also houses a mosque on its top floor, which remains an active place of worship to this day.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Influence:**
 
 
• The Charminar is an exemplary model of Indo-Islamic architecture, blending Persian architectural elements with indigenous Indian styles.
 
• The minarets are 56 meters high and have intricate stucco decorations that add to the beauty of the structure.
 
• The arches are designed in a way to allow the free flow of air, making the structure naturally ventilated.
 
• The structure also features a small water cistern at the center, which was used for ablutions.

questions.question: Net investment can be best expressed using which of the following elements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross Investment - Depreciation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Net investment** represents the total amount invested in an economy minus depreciation.
 
• Depreciation is the reduction in the value of assets over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or other factors.
 
• Gross investment includes all investments made in an economy, without subtracting depreciation.
 
• Therefore, to find the net investment, depreciation must be subtracted from the gross investment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Investment**

 
 
• Gross investment refers to the total amount of money spent on new capital goods, including buildings, machinery, and equipment, within a specific period.
 
• It reflects the total level of investment in an economy without accounting for depreciation.
 
 
 
• **Depreciation**
 
 
• Depreciation is the process of allocating the cost of tangible assets over their useful lives.
 
• It represents how much of an asset's value has been used up over time.
 
• This is an essential accounting method to match the cost of an asset with the revenue it generates.
 
 
 
• **Net Investment**
 
 
• Net investment is calculated by subtracting depreciation from gross investment.
 
• It indicates the actual addition to the capital stock of an economy after accounting for the wear and tear of existing assets.
 
• This measure is crucial for understanding the net increase in the productive capacity of an economy.
 
 
 
• **Replacement Cost**
 
 
• Replacement cost is the amount that an entity would have to pay to replace an asset at the present time, according to its current worth.
 
• It is often used in insurance to determine the value of replacing an insured item.
 
 
 
• **Depletion Value**
 
 
• Depletion is similar to depreciation but applies to natural resources such as minerals, oil, and timber.
 
• It refers to the allocation of the cost of extracting natural resources over the period they are consumed.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of sodium nitrate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NaNO3**__.

__
 
• Sodium nitrate is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula **NaNO3**.
 
• It is a white, crystalline solid that is highly soluble in water.
 
• Sodium nitrate is commonly used in fertilizers, food preservatives, and in the production of explosives.
 
• It is also known as Chile saltpeter due to its large deposits found in Chile.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inorganic Compounds:**

 
 
• These compounds generally do not contain carbon-hydrogen bonds.
 
• They are typically minerals and include salts, metals, and other elemental compounds.
 
 
 
• **Solubility:**
 
 
• The ability of a substance to dissolve in a solvent, such as water.
 
• Sodium nitrate is highly soluble in water, making it useful in various applications.
 
 
 
• **Fertilizers:**
 
 
• Substances that provide essential nutrients to plants to promote growth.
 
• Sodium nitrate supplies nitrogen, which is a crucial nutrient for plant growth.
 
 
 
• **Food Preservatives:**
 
 
• Substances added to food to prevent spoilage and extend shelf life.
 
• Sodium nitrate is used to preserve meats and prevent the growth of harmful bacteria.

questions.question: Geeta Mahalik won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for which form of dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Geeta Mahalik is a renowned Odissi dancer known for her contributions to the classical dance form of Odissi.
 
• She was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for her outstanding performance and contribution to the field of Odissi dance.
 
• Odissi is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Odisha.
 
• The dance form is known for its fluid movements, sculpturesque poses, and intricate footwork, often depicting religious stories and spiritual themes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi Dance**

 
 
• Odissi is one of the oldest surviving dance forms in India, with its origins traced back to ancient temples in Odisha.
 
• It is characterized by three main positions: Samabhanga (equal balance), Tribhanga (three bends), and Chowk (square-like stance).
 
• The dance includes Mangalacharan (invocation), Batu (pure dance), Pallavi (elaborate dance), Abhinaya (expressive dance), and Moksha (salvation).
 
• Odissi dance is often performed to the accompaniment of Odissi music, which is a classical music form of Odisha.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi**
 
 
• Established in 1952, the Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's national academy for music, dance, and drama.
 
• It is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.
 
• The academy's primary objective is to promote and preserve the cultural heritage of India in the field of performing arts.
 
• It confers the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award annually to artists for their outstanding contribution to Indian performing arts.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Dance Forms of India**
 
 
• **Kathakali:** A dance-drama form from Kerala, known for its elaborate costumes, makeup, and face masks.
 
• **Bharatanatyam:** Originating from Tamil Nadu, this dance form is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate hand movements.
 
• **Kuchipudi:** A classical dance form from Andhra Pradesh, characterized by its graceful movements and strong narrative expression.
 
• **Manipuri:** A dance form from Manipur, known for its graceful and fluid movements, depicting themes from the life of Krishna.
 
• **Mohiniyattam:** A classical dance form from Kerala, performed by women and characterized by gentle and graceful movements.

• **Skills Acquisition and Knowledge Awareness for Livelihood Promotion (SANKALP)**
 
 
• SANKALP is an initiative of the Indian government to improve short-term skill training qualitatively and quantitatively.
 
• The programme focuses on promoting market-relevant skills, strengthening institutions, and ensuring better access to skill development opportunities.
 
• SANKALP is a World Bank-supported project aimed at transforming the skill development landscape in India.

• It aims to improve the responsiveness and accountability of public administration.
 
• Decentralisation helps in better addressing local needs and priorities and fosters participatory governance.

questions.question: Who among the following was one of the court poets of the King Samudragupta?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• Samudragupta is often referred to as the "Napoleon of India" due to his extensive military campaigns and conquests.
 
• He was also known for his administrative skills and efforts in promoting trade, commerce, and cultural activities.

• The inscription praises Samudragupta's military prowess, highlighting his conquests and victories over various kingdoms and tribes.
 
• It also mentions his qualities as a ruler, including his administrative abilities, patronage of arts, and benevolence towards his subjects.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles provides the minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 30**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 30** of the Indian Constitution grants minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
 
• This article is part of the Fundamental Rights guaranteed under Part III of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The term "minorities" in Article 30 primarily refers to religious and linguistic minorities.
 
• The article ensures that minorities can preserve and promote their culture and language through their educational institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 29**

 
 
• Article 29 of the Indian Constitution provides that any section of the citizens residing in the territory of India or any part thereof having a distinct language, script, or culture of its own shall have the right to conserve the same.
 
• This article protects the interests of minorities by ensuring that their language, script, or culture is not discriminated against.
 
 
 
• **Article 28**
 
 
• Article 28 deals with the freedom as to attendance at religious instruction or religious worship in certain educational institutions.
 
• No religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.
 
 
 
• **Article 31**
 
 
• Article 31 originally dealt with the right to property but was repealed by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978.
 
• After its repeal, the right to property is no longer a fundamental right but a constitutional right under Article 300A.
